workItem.goal: Present an already-computed dependency comparison in the browser so a person can distinguish and inspect added, removed and changed modules and directed relationships, including side-specific evidence, scope and uncertainty.
workItem.writeBoundary: Only files owned by ramify/presentation/project-view beneath subs/presentation/subs/project-view/src/, excluding module.ramify. This iteration may add or change presentation source, styles and owned tests; it may not write another owner or expose a new module contract.
excludedWork: ramify/explorer page state, baseline selection, save/list/delete controls, refresh orchestration and navigation wiring
ramify/service-api browser transport, DTO projection, paging and result-size enforcement
ramify/daemon persistence, shared baseline lifecycle service and project-context coordination
ramify/analysis comparison computation or changes to dependency meaning
ramify/cli commands, human-readable terminal output and deterministic JSON output
module.ramify changes, new modules, cross-owner contracts and cross-branch writes
end-to-end claims based only on local fixtures

firstIteration.goal: Render a focused comparison summary and selectable change detail from supplied comparison data, with historical/current labeling and explicit incomplete, unavailable and limited states, while adding executable component evidence for the presentation behavior.
acceptance: An owned component test supplies one added module, one removed module, one added relationship, one removed relationship and one relationship whose existing dependency counts or classifications differ; the rendered summary identifies each category without inventing source analysis.

Selecting a changed relationship shows the canonical consumer and provider and labeled before and after values for every supplied count and classification, without flattening the two sides into one value.

Selecting an added or removed module or relationship keeps the existing side inspectable and labels retained evidence as historical or current; absent-side wording does not imply that source still exists.

Each side's analyzed input or revision identity, production dependency scope and coverage state are visible. Partial or unavailable coverage cannot render as a clean no-change result or turn an unobserved relationship into a definite removal.
A supplied no-change comparison renders a clear no-dependency-changes result only when both sides are sufficiently complete; a qualified observation set uses qualified wording instead.
A display filter changes visible rows and labels filtered totals against full supplied totals; it does not mutate the supplied comparison or redefine its scope.
Unavailable, retryable and resource-limit outcomes are distinct, readable states and do not render an empty comparison.

The focused ramify/presentation/project-view component tests and the project TypeScript check pass after the implementation. These are new evidence to establish during the iteration, not evidence that exists now.
requiredEvidence: New focused component tests under subs/presentation/subs/project-view/src/tests/ covering complete, partial, unavailable, retryable and resource-limit states and selectable historical/current detail.
A focused Vitest run for the changed project-view tests.
A diff review confirming every write remains in ramify/presentation/project-view and module.ramify is unchanged.
notCompletionOf: The browser baseline workflow or integration into an explorer page
Baseline save, list, delete, persistence, compatibility or corruption handling
Dependency comparison computation and coherent current-revision selection
The dependency-baselines feature or any provider delegation

Understand the owner's current pure presentation responsibility, dependency meaning and existing state vocabulary.
Confirm ownership and existing exposure without changing the declaration in this iteration.
Reuse the existing visual language, selection/detail behavior, coverage labels and stale/refresh presentation patterns.
Preserve the existing browser dependency counts, classifications, evidence and states rather than redefining dependency meaning.
Reuse canonical module identities, revision identity, source evidence and coverage vocabulary already present in the owner.
Follow the owner's component-test conventions and existing evidence, detail, unavailable and stale cases.
Follow existing fixture conventions while keeping newly authored comparison fixtures explicitly synthetic.
Record that the shared requester API snapshot is revision rev/1:c0f289c6-2132-4574-a035-d16b1f73fd48:4 with complete catalog coverage for this source area.

unresolvedQuestions: What bounded comparison result and detail retrieval states will the service supply?
Which side identities, totals, coverage, retry and resource-limit fields belong in the cross-owner agreement?
Will historical detail be included, paged or requested separately?
Where will comparison selection and detail state live?
How will stale results, refresh, baseline selection and explicit deletion be coordinated?
What deterministic change vocabulary distinguishes definite changes from qualified observations?
What bounded evidence subset preserves historical inspection without retaining a full report or source tree?

localContinuation: Reconcile the first iteration's local presentation input with the reviewed service agreement, replacing any deliberately local test adapter rather than exposing it as a provider contract.
Integrate the comparison presentation with the existing dependency diagram or a distinct comparison mode after that interaction decision is reviewed.
Add comparison-specific navigation, keyboard behavior and larger-data presentation once result/detail bounds are known.
Verify the final component against real service output and browser acceptance after provider and explorer work exists.
rationale: The project-view owner is the leaf browser consumer that determines whether retained before/after facts are understandable and inspectable. A pure supplied-data iteration can produce a visible user outcome and executable evidence without scanning source or implementing a second analyzer.

The iteration is deliberately smaller than the browser work item: it covers comparison summary and detail presentation, while baseline selection, lifecycle controls, refresh orchestration and page integration remain with ramify/explorer.

The terminal is also an essential consumer, but choosing it first would not validate the request's hardest presentation obligation: inspecting removed entities with clearly separated historical and current evidence. Terminal work remains a separate consumer work item and is not dropped.

Starting with ramify/daemon, ramify/analysis or storage was rejected because the protocol requires consumer-first work and a provider-first iteration would fix contracts before a consumer demonstrates the needed information.

Starting with ramify/explorer was rejected because its workflow depends on both service operations and a pure comparison presentation; project-view gives a smaller bounded subtree and keeps cross-branch coordination explicit.
